## Where the content comes from

The app is built from a study guide (`sta520-study-app-guide_1.md`) synthesized from the course's lecture slides (PDF/PPTX), expanded with textbook-level background explanations. The background prose is written independently from general molecular biology, genetics and biostatistics knowledge. It is **not** copied from the assigned textbook (*Principles of Genetics and Molecular Epidemiology*, Gomez-Verjan & Rivero-Segura, eds., Springer 2022).

The quizzes, drills, R exercises, figures, written model answers and the illustrative MR numbers in Lecture 6 were added for this app.

**Added later:** "Lecture 7 - questions.pdf", the instructor's example exercises and possible exam questions. Its 11 questions are on the [Exam practice](exam-practice.qmd) page. The questions are the instructor's; the model answers are written for this app and are not an official answer key. The survival result by cluster (M1 shorter survival, log-rank P = 0.029) in Lecture 7 comes from this document.

## How to read the exam flags

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| <span class="flag-badge flag-instructor">🎯 Instructor-flagged EXAM</span> | The slide carried the literal text "EXAM" from the instructor. **Lecture 7 only.** The course's reading guide confirms: *"The slides with information that we will be testing on the exam are marked with a small text 'EXAM.'"* |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-inferred">📌 Likely exam-relevant (AI-inferred)</span> | An **inference** from what the slides present as a definition, formula, worked numerical example or something repeated across lectures. **Not confirmed by the instructor.** |
| (no badge) | Background or context. Still course content. |

## Course schedule (official rough plan)

STA520 Molecular Epidemiology, 4 credits, Sahlgrenska Academy, University of Gothenburg, autumn 2026 (31 Aug – 2 Oct), taught in English.

| Week | Day 1 | Day 2 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Intro to the biological language of molecular epidemiology; biological macromolecules (proteins, DNA, lipids) | DNA–RNA–Protein |
| 2 | Genetic variation and protein function | From SNP to GWAS |
| 3 | From GWAS to Mendelian randomisation | Computer exercise intro |
| 4 | High-dimensional data (gene expression, GO, clusters), proteomics | Study design, bias and interpretation; computer exercise discussion |
| 5 | Integrating molecular data | Workshop/Seminar |

::: {.callout-warning}
## File-to-session correction
"Lecture 3_genetics.pdf" was actually presented **at the start of the Lecture 4 session**, as a recap ("the same lecture notes as posted for lecture 3"). In this app, Lecture 3 merges "Lecture 3_recap and mutations.pdf" and "Lecture 3_genetics.pdf" by content. The genetics fundamentals (Mendel, LD, SNP arrays, HWE; [Sections 3.6–3.9](lecture3.qmd#t3-6)) were therefore **taught in the Lecture 4 session**, just before "Lecture 4 from SNP to GWAS.pdf". This matters if an exam question refers to material "from lecture 4".
:::

## What is missing

These exist in the course but were **not available** when the study guide was written, so nothing here is built from them:

- The full siNET article (Arvidsson et al., *Modern Pathology* 2018): more methodological detail for Lecture 7.
- Solutions to `Computer exercise1.docx` and `Computer exercise 2.docx`. These are deliberately **not** included: the [Computer exercises: concepts](computer-exercises.qmd) page teaches the ideas behind them on made-up and simulated data, without code or results for the course data.
- Raw exercise data: `Lecture4_ex1.csv`, `jointGwasMc_LDL.txt`, `simulated_LDL.pheno`, `all_hg38_subset.*`, `CAD_Summary_filtered.txt`.
- "STA520 Literature list.pdf" and "STA520 Syllabus.pdf" returned no extractable text (probably scanned), so only "STA520 Course Syllabus.docx" was used for the course context.
- The assigned textbook was deliberately not reproduced (copyright).
- Two uploads of "Lecture 3_recap and mutations.pdf" existed; only one was read. No personal comments or annotations were found in any slide PDF.
- Sessions from week 4 day 2 onward ("Study design, bias and interpretation", "Integrating molecular data", the seminar) have no slides in the guide yet.

If any of these become available, they can be added as new sections or questions.

## Your progress data

Your review status (Not reviewed / Reviewed / Confident) is stored in this browser's localStorage under the key `sta520_topic_status`. It stays between visits on the same browser and device, but not across devices or after clearing site data. Use **Export progress** on the [dashboard](dashboard.qmd) to keep a backup.
